original_question: Let L be a finite non-abelian simple group, and let D be a conjugacy class of involutions in L. Consider the complete graph Γ with vertex set D. Define an equivalence relation ∼ (graph coloring) on the set of edges as follows: (a, b) ∼ (c, d) if and only if |ab| = |cd|. An automorphism of the coloured graph Γ is a permutation τ ∈ SD such that(a, b) ∼ (aτ, bτ) for every edge(a, b). Is it true that the automorphism group of Γ is a subgroup of Aut(L)?
target_in_paper: Problem 21.52 in the section "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)" of The Kourovka Notebook. In the current arXiv version of 1401.0300, this is the exact problem your draft is aiming at, essentially verbatim [Problem 21.52, PDF p. 168 / printed p. 169].
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the official problem almost word-for-word: the hypotheses that L is a finite non-abelian simple group and D is a conjugacy class of involutions; the construction of the complete graph on D; the edge-coloring rule via the order of the product ab; the definition of a color-preserving automorphism as a permutation of D preserving that edge-coloring; and the final question asking whether the resulting automorphism group comes from Aut(L) [Problem 21.52, PDF p. 168 / printed p. 169].
missing_details: A stand-alone version should define S_D explicitly as the symmetric group Sym(D) on the set D.
It should make explicit that the edges of the complete graph are the unordered pairs {a,b} with a,b in D and a != b, even though the paper writes them as (a,b).
It should clarify that |ab| means the group-theoretic order of the element ab in L.

To remove the only real ambiguity in the terse notebook formulation, it should say that the intended containment is in the permutation group induced on D by automorphisms of L that stabilize D setwise (or, equivalently in informal notebook language, that every color-preserving permutation of D is induced by an automorphism of L).

The universal quantification is implicit in the notebook wording and can be made explicit: the question is asked for every finite non-abelian simple group L and every conjugacy class D of involutions in L.
refined_question: For every finite non-abelian simple group L and every conjugacy class D of involutions of L, let Gamma be the complete graph whose vertex set is D, and color each edge {a,b} (with a,b in D and a != b) by the group-theoretic order ord(ab) of the product ab in L. Equivalently, two edges {a,b} and {c,d} have the same color exactly when ord(ab) = ord(cd). Let Aut(Gamma) be the group of all permutations tau in Sym(D) such that ord(ab) = ord(a^tau b^tau) for all distinct a,b in D. Must every element of Aut(Gamma) be induced by an automorphism of L; equivalently, is Aut(Gamma) contained in the permutation group on D induced by the setwise stabilizer of D in Aut(L)?
equivalent_formulation: If, following the notation introduced immediately afterward, one defines for each positive integer t the set Aut_t(Gamma) = {tau in Sym(D) : ord(ab) = t implies ord(a^tau b^tau) = t for all a,b in D}, then the paper explicitly notes that Aut(Gamma) = intersection over t of Aut_t(Gamma). Thus the same question can be phrased as: is intersection_t Aut_t(Gamma) induced on D by a subgroup of Aut(L)?
justification: The cited arXiv item is not a standard single-article paper with a Section 1, Conjecture 1.1, Proposition 1.2, and Theorem 1.3; it is the continuously updated Kourovka Notebook. In the current version, your draft matches Problem 21.52 almost exactly, so the nearest official formulation is simply that problem itself rather than any broader neighboring theme. The only meaningful refinements are minor stand-alone clarifications: defining Sym(D), making the edge set and the meaning of |ab| explicit, and clarifying the natural-action interpretation of the phrase "subgroup of Aut(L)." The nearby Problem 21.53 supplies only auxiliary notation Aut_t(Gamma) and the explicit identity Aut(Gamma) = intersection_t Aut_t(Gamma); it does not replace 21.52 with a broader problem [Problems 21.52 and 21.53, PDF pp. 168-169 / printed pp. 169-170].
